task.description:
WF-02, step 1 — write the design of REQ-104 (the real-Chrome end-to-end kit and the command `npm run e2e` inside `npm run check`) in docs/design/REQ-104-e2e-chrome-kit.md, by the section "Step 1" of docs/workflows/WF-02-development.md. No implementation code in the design: shapes, signatures, tables only.

READ FIRST: the block REQ-104 in docs/requirements.yaml (all 13 criteria; read by id, the file is large), decisions/0107-e2e-real-chrome-in-check.md, decisions/0023 (D2), decisions/0002, docs/quality-bar.md, docs/anti-patterns.md, the gate results handoffs/E2E-20261103-01/step-02b-req-validator.json (its Low remarks M1-M3 are for you to handle in the design) and step-02-req-validator.json. REQ-105/106/107 depend on this kit: read their blocks too so the kit's API serves them (window sizes, themes, languages, console errors, overflow check, `e2e: browser=` / `e2e: file=` lines, clean-up).

IMPORTANT FACTS:
- The block REQ-104 and the decision 0107 are in the working tree, NOT in the tag base/E2E104-20261103-01 (they are uncommitted); the tag is the "before" copy for code and tests. Statements about the current system are measured on a fresh clone of the tag outside the project; statements about the requirement are read from the working tree.
- Feasibility sketch by ORCH (outside the project, Node 22.23.4, macOS, Chrome at /Applications/Google Chrome.app): child_process.spawn of Chrome with `--headless=new --remote-debugging-port=0 --user-data-dir=<temp> --no-first-run --disable-gpu`; the `ws://` address is read from the "DevTools listening on" line on stderr; `fetch http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/list` gives the page target; the global WebSocket of Node 22 speaks the protocol; clicking a button and reading `document.title` worked; a window below about 500 px needs `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`. Make your own sketch for every other statement (Linux flags, the sandbox on the runner, killing the process group, favicon request, theme via `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`, language via `Accept-Language`/`navigator.language` override, console errors via `Runtime.exceptionThrown` and `Log.entryAdded`, horizontal overflow check) and put its location and content in result.prototype.
- Six guard tests turn red when `check` gets a sixth step: HC-02, HC-03, HO-54, PK-7b, LP-3, CTL-13 (the replacement table of REQ-104 lists them); measure the others on the tag again, give file, line, "was → became", and the prohibition must not be weakened.
- Another computer has no Chrome in a CI-like situation: the "Chrome missing" path must FAIL with an understandable message, never skip (Q6).
- Only Node 22 built-ins, no npm package. Tests and the kit live in tools/test/ (decide the file layout; REQ-104 names the files — follow it).

HOW TO WORK: sub-steps small enough to be checked one by one, each with the tests that will turn red; a list of mutants (at least 20, one per trap) with the test that catches each; the table "criterion → test"; the bar section for every item Q1-Q14 and R1-R3; open questions as a list (ORCH answers them with a decisions/ record before the gate) — do not settle a disputed choice by a guess. One agent at a time works on this Mac: keep your trials light (no full `npm test` more than twice; kill every Chrome you start by its process id, never by name pattern; clean your temp folders yourself, only the ones you made).
Do not write the name of any other project into any file (traces).
acceptance_criteria: Every criterion of REQ-104 leads to an element of the design and to a test
Replacement table of earlier guard tests, measured on the tag
Bar section Q1-Q14 and R1-R3 complete
At least 20 mutants, each with the test that catches it

result.summary: Wrote docs/design/REQ-104-e2e-chrome-kit.md (649 lines, 20 sections): a kit of ten modules in tools/test/e2e/kit/ (errors, find-chrome, guards, cdp, cleanup, console, browser, page, index, runner) plus tools/test/e2e/run.js; the command `npm run e2e [-- names]` with the run record; the sixth step of `check`; a stand-in program speaking the protocol; 49 tests (36 in tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js, 13 in tools/test/e2e/smoke.e2e.js) mapped to the 13 criteria; the replacement table of the six guard tests measured on the tag; the bar section Q1-Q14 and R1-R3; 8 build sub-steps with the red tests of each; 54 mutants; 9 open questions O1-O9. Measured on fresh clones of the tag: exactly six guard tests turn red (HC-02, HC-03, HO-54, PK-7b, LP-3, CTL-13), full npm test with all files of the work present = 2136 tests, 2130 pass, 6 fail, 0 skipped, 0 todo, 235.8 s. Findings that the requirement does not state and the design builds in: the default colour scheme of a headless Chrome is the machine's (dark here), so the kit sets light; a launched Chrome survives a killed parent (9 orphan processes measured) so clean-up is by process group plus exit/SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers; an unguarded JSON parse of a protocol frame crashed the sketch process; a favicon 404 line and a page 404 line have the same text (declarations match on text and optional path); without a resolver rule the browser reaches the network (a trial did not finish in 120 s), so --host-resolver-rules leaves only 127.0.0.1. Remarks M1-M3 of the gate: M1 corrected in section 12 row 7, M2 answered by the error codes and the log-reading table in section 6, M3 raised as O4. Not measured and said so: Linux flags, the sandbox on the runner, the resolver rule on Linux (criterion 10 settles them by a real run); I pushed nothing.

issues.text: O1 (ORCH): who writes the starter of server processes (spawn, read a stdout line, SIGTERM and exit code, refuse a state folder outside the temporary root) that REQ-105, 106 and 107 each need? Design default: not in REQ-104 (no criterion, no test); REQ-105 designs tools/test/e2e/kit/stand.js and the others reuse it. REQ-104 provides makeTempDir, removeTempDir, assertUnderTempRoot.

O2 (ORCH): page code as strings only (default) or add globals.browser for test/e2e/** in eslint.config.js and accept functions? Measured: a function with `document` in a spec fails no-undef; eslint.config.js is not in the file list of REQ-104.

O3 (ORCH): confirm the runner rules beyond the letter of criteria 7 and 11: stop at the first failing spec file; a hung file ended after 120 s (SPEC_TIMEOUT); a file with no test (node counts the file itself as one test), or with skipped/todo above 0, fails.

O4 (ORCH, remark M3 of the gate): the hash comparison of the REQ-014 and REQ-033 blocks against tag B in criterion 13 turns red if the owner's answers about those two requirements land in this run. Default: keep their WF-01 runs after the release of this run.

O5 (ORCH): accept the extra Chrome flag --host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND , EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1 (second layer of criterion 5). Measured on this Mac: example.com, the literal 192.0.2.1, localhost and a 302 to example.com all fail at once (ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED) and 127.0.0.1 loads; without it a trial navigating to foreign addresses did not finish in 120 s. Linux behaviour is read by the criterion-10 run (SMK-13).

O6 (ORCH): the stand-in program fake-chrome.js is written by BACKEND-DEV (a stand, as in the design of REQ-056) in sub-step 3 because the fault paths cannot be checked without it; the tests that use it are TEST-DESIGNER's. The REQ owner line gives 'the fault tests' to TEST-DESIGNER.

O7 (ORCH/owner): (a) accept the residual risk that a SIGKILL of the runner (for example a CI job killed at its time limit) leaves Chrome processes (measured: 9 orphans); no sweeper of old sai-e2e-* folders is added. (b) Branch C pre-decision: if the runner log shows that Chrome on ubuntu-24.04 does not start with its sandbox because the system restricts unprivileged user namespaces, may the fix be one step in check.yml that changes that system setting (a runner setting, not a Chrome flag)? Today branch C says BLOCKED with a question to the owner; I could not measure the runner and pushed nothing. (c) FYI: the root README says 'about 2 minutes' for the pre-push check, pinned by RD-2 (repo.test.js 1124); a full npm test alone took 235.8 s, so the sentence was already untrue on the tag.

O8 (ORCH): the kit API offers key presses, network records with response bodies, reload and a second tab, which the description of REQ-104 does not list among 'the kit can' but REQ-105 (criteria 2, 4, 5, 6) and REQ-107 (criterion 4) need. Default: keep, with tests SMK-09 and SMK-11. REVIEWER may read them as work beyond the requirement.

O9 (ORCH, AP-133): the done REQ-038 says (criterion at docs/requirements.yaml line 5313; description 5266-5268) that the check 'check ends with npm run test' in team-web-control.test.js passes without edit. This work edits that assertion (CTL-13), so the statement becomes false. A WF-01 micro-amendment in this run, or a defect? docs/requirements.yaml is not in my write set.

One record decisions/0108-e2e-kit-conventions.md with the section 'Basis', answering O1-O9 before the gate 1b (WF-02 step 1a). ORCH should also put the table 'reading of the CI log' (section 6 of the design: branch B = error=CHROME_NOT_FOUND and no browser= line; branch C = error=START_EXITED or START_TIMEOUT with the word sandbox and no browser= line; any other red = plain FAIL) into the task of step 9 (remark M2 of the gate).

Remark M1 of the gate was right and is applied: the REQ text says the REQ-030 tests read two README sections that the work does not change; the work edits the paragraph 'You need' of the root README and the section 'Check' of tools/README.md. Measured: the tests stay green with both edits (163-test subset and the full npm test show only the six red tests). Section 12 row 7 says so.
The root README.md is not covered by prettier (format:check runs in tools/); running prettier on it rewrote 15 unrelated lines in the clone. The design says: edit the root README by hand.

Not measured, said so in the design: the Linux flags, the Chrome sandbox on the runner, the behaviour of the resolver rule on Linux. The published software list of the ubuntu-24.04 image 20261026.354.1 names Google Chrome 156.0.8078.47 (documentation, read only, not a run).

AP-136 slip, mine: during the sketches the kit-like launcher wrote Chrome profile folders (sai-e2e-*, 5 left over) and stand-in log folders (fk-*, 12) into the system temporary folder instead of the session scratch folder; one stand-in process (pid 75093) survived a crashed sketch (the sketch client died on an unguarded JSON parse, see F25); one sketch (s8) did not finish in 120 s and was stopped with TaskStop. All folders were removed by name and the process killed by its pid; afterwards ps shows no remote-debugging/fake-chrome/sai-e2e- process and the temporary folder holds no sai-e2e-/fk- entry. The design asks later checkers to run the kit with TMPDIR set to their scratch folder.
